rationale: CoMD is a compute-intensive HPC molecular dynamics proxy app whose execution time is dominated by tight floating-point loops (force computation, neighbor-list traversal, integration) with essentially no I/O or parsing, so reverse-engineering resistance must come overwhelmingly from cheap, loop-safe transformations: SUB is weighted as the primary defense (near-zero runtime/size cost, low risk, meaningful gain on arithmetic-heavy code), backed by SPLIT for cheap control-flow diversity; FLA is allowed at moderate weight so it lands mostly on cold driver routines (main, setup, command-line handling) rather than hot kernels, while BCF's inflated straight-line loop bodies are exactly what must be avoided in this profile, so it carries low security/diversity weights and high runtime/size costs to confine it to rare, cold functions; IBR and ICALL are kept at moderate-low weights since CoMD's indirect-branch/call surface is small and indirect dispatch inside hot loops defeats branch prediction, and IGV is mildly favored because CoMD keeps simulation state in module-level globals whose indirection costs little outside the innermost loops; CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low across the board because the static profile gives no function-level features to gate on, so risk must be minimized by construction (favoring semantics-preserving arithmetic/substitution passes over aggressive control-flow restructuring).
